events.age: One-Time Events | Join us for a special The World & Me as we celebrate unique movement and patterns on the planet we call home with local dancers from Company | E , musicians from Sound Impact , and educators from the National Museum of Natural History. events.name: History Film Forum presents Faith on Film: American Muslims
events.age: One-Time Events | The History Film Forum presents two episodes from the 2026 PBS documentary series “American Muslims: A History Revealed.” The 2026 PBS documentary series “American Muslims: A History Revealed” is six short documentary films that explores the early history of Muslims in America. The series is hosted by three American Muslim journalists: Malika Bilal, Aymann Ismail and Asma Khalid who traveled the country to piece together stories spanning over 200 years. The two episodes, “A Portrait of Freedom” and “Islam at the Nation’s Founding,” will be shown in a special edited version as part of an exploration of Muslim American history in the early United States. A panel discussion will follow the screening. This program is presented in partnership with the museum’s Center for the Understanding of Religion in American History, which explores the influence of religion on every facet of life in the United States. “Faith on Film” is in an ongoing series exploring belief on screen, from the golden age of cinema to binge-worthy shows of the streaming era. Through classics like “The Ten Commandments” and “Yentl” and recent fan favorites including “The Chosen” and “Never Have I Ever,” Hollywood's view of religion has long shaped American culture. The National Museum of American History welcomes visitors of all ages and abilities. This event is wheelchair accessible. Captioning and assistive listening devices will be provided. Additional accommodations are available upon request; please email nmahprograms@si.edu . Two weeks’ notice is preferred. Seating is limited and reservations are recommended. Seating will be opened first to Eventbrite-registered attendees and then to walk-in visitors. events.name: The Seoul Guardians
events.age: Films | Joie Chen, an Emmy-winning anchor and correspondent formerly of CNN, Al Jazeera, and CBS News will join directors Kim Jong-woo, Kim Shin-wan, and Cho Chul-young for an onstage conversation after the screening. Watch the Trailer On the night of December 3, 2024, then-president Yoon Suk Yeol declared martial law in Korea. He banned all political activities and public assemblies and sent troops to the National Assembly building to seize control. The Seoul Guardians plunges you into the political chaos of that night, with codirecting by three journalists who were there. Lawmakers rush to pass a bill ending martial law as ordinary citizens band together to hold off the soldiers sent to take the building. The winner of multiple film festival awards, this stirring documentary resonates with audiences around the world with its message that democracy is fragile and must be defended. Directors: Kim Jong-woo, Kim Shin-wan, and Cho Chul-young. Country: Korea. Released: 2026. Length: 70 min. Format: DCP. Language: Korean with English subtitles.
